fixes.explanation: Close, friend, but Paul actually goes the other way. Paul, the apostle writing this letter to Timothy, opens with "This is a trustworthy saying: If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task." That's no warning label. He calls the task noble.

Fear of man feels like it belongs on a list like this, and I'd have guessed it too. I get jumpy every time a fresh batch comes out of the oven. But it isn't on Paul's list here. In verse 3 he says an overseer must be "…free of the love of money."

That's a nice thought, but Paul never says it. What he asks is a question: if someone does not know how to manage his own household, "…how can he care for the church of God?" Family helping to lead isn't in the verse.

Paul doesn't mention a meeting place in this verse. What he asks is a question: if someone does not know how to manage his own household, "…how can he care for the church of God?" That question is the reason he gives in verse 5.

Careless sounds right, like forgetting the oven mitt, but it isn't what Paul writes. He says the recent convert "…may become conceited and fall under the same condemnation as the devil" (1 Timothy 3:6). The word he uses is conceited.
I can see why you'd pick it, but elected isn't Paul's word. He says deacons "…must first be tested." Then, if they are above reproach, they serve. So the test comes before serving as a deacon.

Lazy isn't in this verse, friend. Paul says the women must be "…dignified, not slanderers, but temperate and faithful in all things." The word he uses is slanderers. If lazy were on the list, my snooze button and I would be in big trouble.

Fearful feels like it should fit, and I'd have said it too. I once jumped when my own apron string tapped me. But Paul says the women must be "…dignified, not slanderers, but temperate and faithful in all things." The word in the verse is slanderers.
Right, it's false. The confession says He "…was proclaimed among the nations, was believed in throughout the world…" That reaches far past Israel. Paul's line names the nations and the world.
